question: Is exempt income the same as a tax deduction?
answer: No. A tax deduction reduces taxable income; exempt income is excluded from taxable income altogether.

question: What allowances or incomes are exempt from income tax?
answer: Examples include: income of listed First Schedule institutions; income of persons with Diplomatic Privilege Act immunities; official income of foreign public servants paid from and taxed in their country; allowances paid abroad to Ugandan foreign mission staff; all income of local authorities; income of URA-certified exempt organisations except unrelated business/property income; bona fide education grants; court-ordered alimony/allowance; gifts/bequests/inheritance not forming business/employment/property income; capital gains outside business (except on private company shares or commercial buildings); technical assistance employment income (non-resident or resident solely for that work, with ministerial concurrence); foreign-source income of short-term residents/foreign public servants/technical assistance staff and immediate family; pensions; lump-sum from resident retirement fund to member/dependent; life insurance proceeds; official employment income of UPDF/UPF/ESO/ISO/Prisons (non-civilian); MP employment income except salary; DPP prosecutors’ employment income; income of GoU and other governments; Bank of Uganda income; collective investment scheme income distributed to participants; EADB employee emoluments; investor compensation fund income; deposit protection fund income; income of aircraft operators in domestic/international traffic; income of exporters of finished consumer and capital goods (subject to conditions); sports awards for winning/participating; SACCO income; income from letting/leasing in industrial park/free zone (conditions); income of operators in industrial park/free zone (conditions); interest on infrastructure bonds; dividends of companies created via stock exchange listing.
